# mypy plugin features

<!-- Generated by `plugin_features_doc.py` from the plugin module docstrings, do not edit. -->

## Annotations

### Add the names given to `QuerySet.annotate()` and `alias()` to the model type

```python
reveal_type(Book.objects.annotate(n=Count("id")).get().n)  # int
Book.objects.annotate(title=F("id"))  # error: Attribute "title" already defined on "Book"  [no-redef]
```

`alias()` names are typed as instance attributes too, although Django doesn't set them.

### Keep annotations through custom `QuerySet` methods returning `WithAnnotations`

```python
class BookQuerySet(models.QuerySet[_M]):
    def with_price(self) -> "BookQuerySet[WithAnnotations[_M, PriceDict]]": ...

book = Book.objects.annotate(n=Count("id")).with_price().get()
reveal_type(book.price)  # int
reveal_type(book.n)  # int
```

### Infer the output type of a `Func` expression from its `output_field`

```python
book = Book.objects.annotate(raw=Substr("title", 1, 10, output_field=BinaryField())).get()
reveal_type(book.raw)  # bytes | memoryview[int]
```

## App registry

Narrows `apps.get_model()` to the referenced model.
With literal arguments, the model class is returned instead of `type[Any]`.

```python
reveal_type(apps.get_model("myapp.Book"))  # type[Book]
apps.get_model("myapp.Missing")  # error: Could not match lazy reference with any model  [misc]
```

Migration `apps` (`StateApps`) keep `type[Any]`, since their models are historical.

## Auth user model

Resolves `get_user_model()`, `request.user` and other auth APIs to `AUTH_USER_MODEL`.

```python
# settings.py: AUTH_USER_MODEL = "myapp.MyUser"
reveal_type(get_user_model())  # type[MyUser]
reveal_type(request.user)  # MyUser | AnonymousUser
```

## Choices

Narrows the value and label types of `Choices` enums.
`choices`, `values`, `labels`, `value` and `label` follow the enum definition,
and `__empty__` adds `None` to the values.

```python
class Gender(models.TextChoices):
    MALE = "M", "Male"
    __empty__ = "(Undeclared)"

reveal_type(Gender.choices)  # list[tuple[str | None, str]]
reveal_type(Gender.MALE.label)  # str
```

## Field lookups

Type-checks lookups passed to `filter()`, `get()`, `exclude()` and friends.
Also covers `get_or_create()`, `update_or_create()` and the async variants.

```python
Book.objects.filter(nope=1)  # error: Cannot resolve keyword 'nope' into field. Choices are: id, title  [misc]
Book.objects.get(id=Book())  # error: Incompatible type for lookup 'id': (got "Book", expected "str | int")  [misc]
```

## Field name validation

Field names passed as strings are resolved like Django does at runtime, async variants included:

| Method | Accepts |
| --- | --- |
| `select_related()` | foreign key and one-to-one relations |
| `order_by()`, `earliest()`, `latest()` | fields, relations, transforms like `__year` and annotations |
| `distinct()` | like `order_by()`, without the `-` prefix |
| `defer()`, `only()` | fields and relations |
| `update()` | concrete fields |
| `in_bulk(field_name=...)` | unique fields, or the field the queryset is `distinct()` on |
| `bulk_update(fields=...)`, `bulk_create(update_fields=...)` | concrete fields other than the primary key |
| `bulk_create(unique_fields=...)` | concrete fields |
| `Model.save(update_fields=...)` | concrete fields other than the primary key |

```python
Book.objects.select_related("title")  # error: Invalid field name "title" in select_related lookup. ...  [misc]
Book.objects.latest("nope")  # error: Cannot resolve keyword 'nope' into field. Choices are: ...  [misc]
Book.objects.distinct("-title")  # error: Cannot resolve keyword '-title' into field. Choices are: ...  [misc]
Book.objects.update(tags=1)  # error: "update()" can only be used with concrete fields. Got "tags"  [misc]
Book.objects.in_bulk(field_name="title")  # error: "in_bulk()"'s field_name must be a unique field ...  [misc]
book.save(update_fields=["id"])  # error: "save()" does not support primary key fields. Got "id"  [misc]
```

## Forms

Allows combining forms whose nested `Meta` classes differ.
A form's `Meta` is typed as `Any`, so inheriting from several forms isn't reported as an incompatible definition.

```python
class CompositeForm(ArticleForm, CategoryForm): ...  # no error
```

## Generic subclasses

Keeps custom subclasses declared without type arguments generic:

- `QuerySet` subclasses over their model and row types
- `Manager` subclasses over their model and queryset
- `Field` subclasses over their value types

```python
class BookQuerySet(models.QuerySet): ...
class BookManager(models.Manager): ...
class HTMLField(models.TextField): ...

class Book(models.Model):
    summary = HTMLField(null=True)
    objects = BookManager()
    published = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

reveal_type(Book.published.all())  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
reveal_type(Book.objects.get())  # Book
reveal_type(Book().summary)  # str | None
```

Skipped under `disallow_any_generics = true`, which requires the type arguments.

## HTTP requests

Reports mutations of immutable `QueryDict`s such as `request.GET`.

```python
request.GET["page"] = "2"  # error: This QueryDict is immutable.  [misc]
params = request.GET.copy()
params["page"] = "2"  # OK
```

## Managers

### Infer the model of a manager instantiated in a model body

So `objects = BookManager()` needs no annotation.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookManager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # BookManager[Book, QuerySet[Book, Book]]
```

### Resolve `QuerySet` methods on managers built by `from_queryset()` and `as_manager()`

Custom methods are bound to the model, and built-in ones return your queryset class.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = models.Manager.from_queryset(BookQuerySet)()

reveal_type(Book.objects.filter(id=1))  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
```

### Create a manager class for a module-level `Manager.from_queryset()`

```python
BookManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(BookQuerySet)

class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookManager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # ManagerFromBookQuerySet[Book, BookQuerySet[Book, Book]]
```

### Type `QuerySet.as_manager()` as a manager with the queryset's methods

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # ManagerFromBookQuerySet[Book, BookQuerySet[Book, Book]]
reveal_type(Book.objects.published())  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
```

### Add the related model's manager methods to reverse `ForeignKey` and `ManyToManyField` managers

Many-to-many managers get them on both sides of the relation.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    publisher = models.ForeignKey(Publisher, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="books")
    authors = models.ManyToManyField(Author)
    objects = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

reveal_type(Publisher().books.published())  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
reveal_type(Book().authors.active())  # AuthorQuerySet[Author, Author], from Author's default manager
```

## Model classes

### Report `objects` and `DoesNotExist` accessed where Django doesn't add them

Django adds `objects` to concrete models only, and `DoesNotExist` and friends to `Model` subclasses only.

```python
def count(model: type[models.Model]) -> None:
    model.objects.count()  # error: "type[Model]" has no attribute "objects"  [attr-defined]
```

Set `strict_model_abstract_attrs = false` to allow it, at your own risk: `count(models.Model)` fails at runtime.

### Add the attributes Django generates on model classes

Such as `id` and `pk`, `<fk>_id`, managers, reverse relations, `get_<field>_display()` and `DoesNotExist`.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    publisher = models.ForeignKey(Publisher, on_delete=models.CASCADE)

reveal_type(Book().publisher_id)  # int
reveal_type(Publisher().book_set)  # RelatedManager[Book, QuerySet[Book, Book]]
```

### Resolve `WithAnnotations[Model, TypedDict]` to the annotated model type

Use it to type instances returned by `annotate()`.

```python
def f(book: WithAnnotations[Book, Pages]) -> None:
    reveal_type(book.n_pages)  # int, from the `Pages` TypedDict
```

## Model fields

Infers the value type of model fields from their arguments.
`null=True` adds `None`, and related fields resolve their target model, even given as a string.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    subtitle = models.CharField(max_length=100, null=True)
    publisher = models.ForeignKey("Publisher", on_delete=models.CASCADE)

reveal_type(Book().subtitle)  # str | None
reveal_type(Book().publisher)  # Publisher
```

## Model instantiation

Type-checks the arguments of `Model(...)`, `QuerySet.create()` and `QuerySet.acreate()`.

```python
Book(pages=[])  # error: Incompatible type for "pages" of "Book" (got "list[Any]", ...)  [misc]
Book(author="Herbert")  # error: Unexpected attribute "author" for model "Book"  [misc]
Book.objects.create(author="Herbert")  # error: Unexpected attribute "author" for model "Book"  [misc]
await Book.objects.acreate(author="Herbert")  # error: Unexpected attribute "author" for model "Book"  [misc]
```

## Model options (`_meta`)

Infers the field returned by `Model._meta.get_field()`.

```python
reveal_type(Book._meta.get_field("publisher"))  # ForeignKey[Publisher, Publisher]
Book._meta.get_field("nope")  # error: Book has no field named 'nope'  [misc]
```

## Prefetching

Type-checks `QuerySet.prefetch_related()` and adds `Prefetch(to_attr=...)` attributes to the model type.

```python
book = Book.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("tags", Tag.objects.all(), to_attr="tag_list")).get()
reveal_type(book.tag_list)  # list[Tag]
Book.objects.prefetch_related("nope")  # error: Cannot find "nope" on "Book" object, ...  [misc]
```

`Prefetch()` keeps its `lookup` and `to_attr` as literal types,
so a `Prefetch` stored in a variable still adds its `to_attr` in `prefetch_related()`.

```python
tags = Prefetch("tags", Tag.objects.all(), to_attr="tag_list")
reveal_type(tags)  # Prefetch[Literal['tags'], QuerySet[Tag, Tag], Literal['tag_list']]
```

## Settings

Infers `django.conf.settings` attribute types from your settings module, falling back to Django's defaults.

```python
reveal_type(settings.BASE_DIR)  # Path
settings.NOT_EXISTING  # error: 'Settings' object has no attribute 'NOT_EXISTING'  [misc]
```

Set `strict_settings = false` to type settings only created at runtime as `Any` instead of reporting them.

## `values()` and `values_list()` row types

Infers the row type returned by `QuerySet.values()` and `QuerySet.values_list()`,
including `flat=True` and `named=True`.

```python
reveal_type(Book.objects.values("title", n=Count("id")).get())  # TypedDict({'title': str, 'n': int})
reveal_type(Book.objects.values_list("title", "pages").get())  # tuple[str, int]
reveal_type(Book.objects.values_list("title", flat=True).get())  # str
Book.objects.values("nope")  # error: Cannot resolve keyword 'nope' into field. Choices are: ...  [misc]
```
